title: AI materially assists AI R&D
claim: Frontier AI systems can perform materially useful portions of the research and engineering work involved in developing AI systems, under human direction or supervision.

supportingEvidence.name: Anthropic
supportingEvidence.summary: Its internal R&D Automation Index reports Claude at collaborates level or above for more than 90% of measured AI R&D work and leads 26%. Anthropic reports no measured subset as fully autonomous.

supportingEvidence.name: OpenAI
supportingEvidence.summary: Its research organization reports using 3.1 agent-workdays for every human workday, with coding agents increasingly integrated into research workflows.

supportingEvidence.name: METR RE-Bench
supportingEvidence.summary: Independent evaluations show frontier agents can perform challenging ML research-engineering tasks, while substantial gaps relative to expert humans remain at longer time horizons.

supportingEvidence.name: Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve
supportingEvidence.summary: AI-generated algorithms have been used in Google infrastructure and AI training processes, including training models underlying AlphaEvolve itself.

limitations: Material assistance is not universal productivity acceleration. METR's randomized 2025 study of experienced open-source developers found developers took 19% longer when allowed to use then-current AI tools. METR's later study produced raw evidence pointing toward speedup, but selection effects prevented a reliable estimate. Frontier-lab measurements are also partly self-reported and should not be treated as equivalent to independent replication.
assessment: Established — high confidence. Convergent evidence from frontier-lab deployment, independent evaluation and concrete algorithmic contributions establishes that AI can materially assist portions of AI R&D. This does not establish autonomous end-to-end AI research, universal productivity gains, sustained recursive self-improvement or an intelligence explosion.
changeTest: A downgrade to Emerging would require substantial independent evidence that apparent AI R&D contributions are systematically offset by verification, correction or integration costs, together with evidence that internal lab measurements materially overstate useful contribution. Evidence of autonomous end-to-end development of materially improved successor systems would bear directly on higher rungs.

additionalSources.name: METR — Experienced open-source developer productivity study

history.note: Initial evidence record published. Classification: Established · High confidence.
